To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

teachers' reflections on teaching engineering in the after school club reveal that they navigated boundary crossing to become familiar with engineering content and processes and to mediate their experiences in the after school engineering club.

teachers' experiences in an after school engineering club led to a shift in their teacher identity, as they drew on and expanded upon existing teacher identities to navigate boundary crossing and broker engineering content to students.

veteran teachers in an after school engineering club drew on and expanded their teacher identities in order to navigate the boundary crossings between their existing and emerging teacher identities as they brokered their way through the process of learning about engineering.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways that teachers' identities are shaped by their experiences with new content.
how veteran teachers navigate boundary crossing and broker their experiences with new STEM content and practices.
how teachers make sense of their experiences with new STEM content and how they draw from and expand upon their identities to teach engineering.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the teachers in this study were able to successfully navigate the unfamiliar territory of teaching engineering by leveraging their prior knowledge and skills, and that the engineering design process was a valuable vehicle for them to engage students in authentic, meaningful engineering experiences.
teachers' experiences with engineering content, processes, and practices are mediated by their teacher identity, and that this teacher identity is a dynamic and evolving process.
the teachers' experiences of teaching engineering in the after school engineering club were characterized by a complex interweaving of boundary crossing and brokering.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the teachers' experiences with engineering were shaped by their prior knowledge of teaching and their prior knowledge of the engineering process.

teachers' experiences with teaching unfamiliar STEM content and practices can be understood through the lenses of broking and boundary crossing, as teachers navigate their identities in relation to the content, their teaching, and their students' learning.
teachers' identities and their ability to navigate the boundaries of teaching engineering are key components to the success of engineering instruction in elementary school settings.
The main takeaway from our work is that

teachers' experiences in learning about engineering and teaching engineering can be enhanced through the use of a community of practice that supports teachers in their learning and development of engineering pedagogy.
teachers' identities are fluid and can change over time, especially as they are challenged to learn new content and processes in order to teach engineering in elementary school settings.
teacher identity is a dynamic process that is influenced by the teachers' experiences and interactions with the engineering content, their peers, and the children in their care.
